profile.investigation_focus: Three-section warehouse: north-south selective racking in the west (top beam 5.23 m), racking turned 90 degrees in the north-east (top beam 2.61 m), and floor block-stacking in the south-east where the same pallet is stacked one, two and three high. The map declares the storage ZONES; what is inside them is not in the map and changes between stock states, so the drivable map carries no visibility information. Five cameras, no mirrored pair. Generated by experiments/warehouse_v2_sketches/make_world.py.

task.name: fusion_network_traverse
task.description: Primary fusion traverse for the six-arm fusion comparison: the west dock door, 3.4 m from camera A, to the east cross aisle under camera D. Every arm drives this one route, so the only thing that differs between arms is how the cameras' readings are combined. The start moved here from aisle A2|A3's south mouth on 2026-08-26 because that start left camera A with 4.8 m and camera C with 1.4 m of the traverse: on this route all five cameras contribute (A 7.2, B 14.0, C 3.4, D 17.2, E 18.6 m at a 25% commissioned usable-sighting rate or better) and the number of simultaneously watching cameras spans 0 to 4, which is the axis the fusion arms are compared along. Of the 30.4 m, 2.6 m expects no camera, 9.4 m one, 9.2 m two, 5.0 m three and 4.4 m four. The lane geometry offers six corridor-distinct candidates (30.4-35.0 m); the shortest is driven, and the choice is stated rather than optimised because route choice is not the treatment in this experiment. Camera C is a corner camera looking south-east across the west aisles: the candidates that give it 9-21 m spend their length in the single-camera west aisles and collapse the two-plus-camera share from 61% to 21-26%, so C's share is 3.4 m by deliberate trade.
